content:
I'm working on a formalization of direct limits of directed systems of C∗C^*C∗-algebras. My current approach is to construct the limit as
UniformSpace.Completion (DirectLimit G f).

I have a working version, but before turning more of it into PRs, I'd like feedback on a design question.

To define normed structures on DirectLimit G f, I need assumptions expressing that the transition maps preserve the norm. What would be the idiomatic way in mathlib to represent this?

The options I've considered are roughly:

  • an explicit non-typeclass argument saying that each transition map preserves norm. In my attempt this made downstream typeclass inference awkward, especially when later instances depend on earlier instances that themselves require these explicit assumptions. Maybe there is a way to make this clean that I am missing.
  • a typeclass saying that all maps in a given directed system preserve norm. This seems maybe too specific/ad hoc.
  • an assumption of the form [∀ i j h, IsNormPreservingMap (f i j h)], using a (new) typeclass on individual maps.
  • an assumption of the form [∀ i j h, NormPreservingMapClass (T h) (G i) (G j)] using a (new) typeclass on the types of maps T h. This seems like it would work for for the code defining the instances on the direct limits, and would most closely resemble what is in Mathlib/Algebra/Colimit/DirectLimit.lean, but seems like using the resulting construction would be awkward because it would require defining types T h for maps that preserve norm in addition to whatever other structure?

In the first case, if there is a way to make things clean while using explicit assumptions, another possible route is to, rather than starting from [∀ i, Norm (G i)] plus norm-preserving maps, instead start from [∀ i, NormedAddGroup (G i)] with transition maps satisfying Isometry. Then the norm on the direct limit could be defined from dist x 0. This would cover the C∗C^*C∗-algebra use case, but it feels a bit less general.

What's the expected/preferred approach in mathlib for this sort of situation?

Can you not simply use docs#IsometryClass as an assumption? There won't be any type that currently satisfies all of docs#AlgHomClass, docs#StarHomClass and docs#IsometryClass (besides docs#StarAlgEquiv, which would be useless). But we could either (1) create IsometryStarAlgHom, or (2) create StarAlgEmbedding (which takes a proof of injectivity) and for C⋆-algebras this type will satisfy docs#IsometryClass.
Probably (2) is the most natural thing to do for now.
By the way, whenever you create this PR, please ping me for review.

Ah, I missed that class (IsometryClass) somehow. Thanks, that should work. I should have looked harder for something like that.
WIll do, thanks!

Following up: using [∀ i j h, IsometryClass (T h) (G i) (G j)] worked well. I now have instances of MetricSpace, NormedAddGroup, and NormedAddCommGroup for DirectLimit G f, using that assumption, plus variable [∀ i j h, AddMonoidHomClass (T h) (G i) (G j)] for the additive group instances. (Also the obvious lemmas relating the metric and norm on the direct limit to the ones at the finite stages.)

Before opening a PR, I have two design/file-placement questions.

First, where should this live? I don’t think it should go in Mathlib/Algebra/Colimit/DirectLimit.lean, since that would make the algebraic direct limit file import metric/normed-space material. My current guess would be a new file such as Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Group/DirectLimit.lean, with the metric part either there or possibly in a separate Mathlib/Topology/MetricSpace/DirectLimit.lean.

Second, I noticed Mathlib/Topology/MetricSpace/Gluing.lean already has Metric.InductiveLimit for sequential systems of metric spaces indexed by ℕ (and using Isometry rather than IsometryClass). The construction using DirectLimit is more general and puts metric/normed instances on the existing algebraic DirectLimit G f for directed systems. Should I just mention the relationship in the module docstring for now, or would maintainers expect some compatibility theorem/comparison with Metric.InductiveLimit?

Does this sound like a reasonable PR scope, or would it be preferable to separate the metric-space part from the normed-group part?

isn't DirectLimit an instance of #mathlib4 > Mathlib's morphism hierarchy @ 💬 , meaning we should be trying to replace the {T : ⦃i j : ι⦄ → i ≤ j → Sort u_8} (f : (i j : ι) → (h : i ≤ j) → T h) [⦃i j : ι⦄ → (h : i ≤ j) → FunLike (T h) (F i) (F j)] with a (f : (i j : ι) → (h : i ≤ j) → F i → F j)
Yes, I would make new files as you suggested, and the locations seem reasonable (both Analysis and Topology).

Aaron, I think I'm less concerned about this because DirectLimit is a type, so you won't be trying to rewrite the f ever. Moreover, in practice, you will only have f being a family of morphisms for a certain fixed type of morphism.
As for Metric.InductiveLimit, I think it's fine to add your generalization, and then later we can refactor the Gluing file to use it instead.
A downside of Aaron's suggestion is that anywhere the type appears it will now print as DirectLimit F (fun (x1 x2 : ι) (x3 : x1 ≤ x2) => ⇑(f x1 x2 x3) instead of DirectLimit F f

Jireh Loreaux said:

and then later we can refactor the Gluing file to use it instead.

Let's write a TODO in that file to this effect

Jireh Loreaux said:

Moreover, in practice, you will only have f being a family of morphisms for a certain fixed type of morphism.

what does this mean? are you saying DirectLimit will only ever be used with one specific morphism type?

Aaron Liu said:

isn't DirectLimit an instance of #mathlib4 > Mathlib's morphism hierarchy @ 💬 , meaning we should be trying to replace the {T : ⦃i j : ι⦄ → i ≤ j → Sort u_8} (f : (i j : ι) → (h : i ≤ j) → T h) [⦃i j : ι⦄ → (h : i ≤ j) → FunLike (T h) (F i) (F j)] with a (f : (i j : ι) → (h : i ≤ j) → F i → F j)

another thing with this is that currently we can't take the DirectLimit of a family of functions, since plain functions aren't an instance of FunLike
No, I just mean that if you want a ring structure, you'll want ring homomorphisms. There's not much reason to switch them around.
Alright, I opened the PR for the MetricSpace and NormedAddGroup instances for DirectLimit (using IsometryClass) here : #39673
Looks good, I added some comments
Thanks @Matthew Corbelli ! I'm very excited to have direct limits of C*-algebras!
One possible concern; is there a natural Topology / Bornology / UniformSpace on the direct limit, and does it coincide with the one induced by the metric?
In a perfect world we'd inherit those structures first and show that the metric ones coincide (using all the extra fields of docs#PseudoMetricSpace)
In a pragmatic one we should leave that as TODO in a module docstring somewhere
:thinking: I think the topology induced by a direct limit of uniform spaces may not agree with the direct limit of topological spaces.

Oh, I did encounter some issues along those lines in my other code that I'm adapting to make these PRs. There, I used (perhaps a hack?)

noncomputable local instance (priority := high) : TopologicalSpace (DirectLimit G f) :=
  PseudoMetricSpace.toUniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace

(This wasn't needed to get the instance of CStarRing (DirectLimit G f), but for the IsTopologicalRing )
Where did the topology otherwise come from?

It was getting it from instTopologicalSpaceQuotient in Topology/Constructions.lean .
(Though, this was in a separate project using a version of mathlib from back in March, so idk if that is what it would get using the current version)
Ah, then I think you are in trouble

As I comment in the PR, your goal is to either make the following pass or be un-stateable:

example : (UniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace : TopologicalSpace (DirectLimit G f)) = instTopologicalSpaceQuotient :=
  rfl
I can't comment on whether docs#instTopologicalSpaceQuotient is the right topology

Jireh Loreaux said:

:thinking: I think the topology induced by a direct limit of uniform spaces may not agree with the direct limit of topological spaces.

in fact, it is possible for the direct limit topology of a family of uniform spaces to not agree with the topology induced by any uniformity
Would this be a good addition to CounterExamples?

I’m currently not seeing what the route would be toward making that statement un-stateable.

Since DirectLimit is defined as a quotient, it seems difficult to prevent instTopologicalSpaceQuotient from applying whenever the stages have topologies. And similarly, once there is a UniformSpace coming from PseudoMetricSpace, UniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace also seems unavoidable.

I briefly wondered about putting the metric/uniform structures on a wrapper around DirectLimit instead of on DirectLimit itself, but that seems like it would make the existing algebraic API much harder to use together with the metric/normed one.

I also currently don’t see a route to making the two topologies definitionally equal.
Well, if they are propositionally equal, there's an easy way to handle the defeq problem. But are they? I guess maybe so since we have isometries everywhere?

Matthew Corbelli said:

I’m currently not seeing what the route would be toward making that statement un-stateable.

It would be to either make DirectLimit so that it doesn't inherit the quotient topology, or disable the quotient topology as being an automatic instance

Indeed, making them defeq is easy if they're propeq; this isn't an area I'm super familiar with, but Gemini suggested that we're only in the clear here if the spaces are finite dimensional or the chains are finite.
I'm a bit dubious about docs#DirectLimit being an abbrev.

I believe I have a counterexample showing that they are not always propositionally equal:

Consider the directed system
Z↪2−1Z↪2−2Z↪⋯\mathbb{Z} \hookrightarrow 2^{-1}\mathbb{Z} \hookrightarrow 2^{-2}\mathbb{Z} \hookrightarrow \cdotsZ↪2−1Z↪2−2Z↪⋯
with the usual metrics (or, if you like, the usual NormedAddCommGroups).
Each stage has the discrete topology, so the direct-limit topology on the direct limit (i.e. the final topology for all the of i maps) is discrete.
But the induced metric on the direct limit is the usual metric on the dyadic rationals, whose topology is not discrete.
So the topology induced by the direct-limit (pseudo)metric does not in general coincide with the existing TopologicalSpace instance on DirectLimit (i.e. with the direct limit in the category of topological spaces.)

(There is also a variant of this counterexample using Q=lim→⁡1nZ\mathbb{Q}= \varinjlim \frac{1}{n} \mathbb{Z}Q=lim​n1​Z where the nnn are ordered by divisibility.)

(I believe I can show that the direct limit topology will always be at least as fine as the topology from the direct limit metric)

Eric Wieser said:

Would this be a good addition to CounterExamples?

I have created a counterexample, which is in two parts. First, show that any topological space which is docs#T2Space and docs#CompactlyCoherentSpace but not docs#CompletelyRegularSpace can create a counterexample, and then I have to explicitly construct a topological space satisfying those conditions (I chose the Golomb space).
however, the part where I show the Golomb space satisfies the conditions ended up being more than half the file
I think the Golomb space with its properties should be in counterexamples at least, and perhaps in mathlib

My understanding is that the existing TopologicalSpace instance on DirectLimit (coming from the quotient topology) is the topology obtained by taking the direct limit in the category of topological spaces and continuous maps, and as such is the topology that one would, in some contexts, want.

However, the dyadic-rationals example shows that this topology can differ from the topology induced by the natural direct-limit metric/pseudometric.

On a blackboard, if someone writes lim→⁡G\varinjlim Glim​G for a directed system GGG of metric spaces with isometric maps, I would expect the metric topology, whereas for GGG a directed system in the category of topological spaces and continuous maps, I would expect the direct-limit/final topology.

As these can differ, I’m not sure what the preferred design is here.

Would you prefer that I:

  • define the PseudoMetricSpace/MetricSpace instances on a separate wrapper type rather than directly on DirectLimit,
  • try making DirectLimit a def rather than an abbrev, so that it no longer automatically inherits the quotient topology,
    • or achieve this in some other way? (how?)
  • somehow(?) disable, in this situation, the quotient topology from being found by the typeclass search,
  • something else?
